project-charter.title: Project Charter

cards.title: Real-World Industrial Scenario
cards.body: At Kirloskar Pump Systems, Pune, a heavy-duty industrial centrifugal water pump is driven by a 22 kW electric motor at 1440 rpm through a 40 mm diameter solid steel transmission shaft. Power is transferred from the shaft to the pump impeller hub using a standard sunken parallel square key (width b = 10 mm, height h = 10 mm, installed length l = 45 mm). During recent continuous pumping operations under fluctuating head conditions, repeated micro-slippage and fretting wear were reported along the keyway. As a Senior Mechanical Design Engineer, you are assigned to evaluate the torque transmission mechanics, verify shear and crushing stress limits, determine the factor of safety, and recommend a safe, reliable key design.

cards.title: Role & Assignment Scope
cards.body: As a Mechanical Design Engineer, you must analyze the shaft-hub-key connection, determine transmitted torque T and tangential force Ft, calculate actual shear and crushing stresses, evaluate Factor of Safety (FOS), identify the governing failure mode, and formulate evidence-based design recommendations.

engineering-context.title: Engineering Context

cards.title: Shaft-Hub-Key Connection Mechanics
cards.body: A key is a temporary demountable machine element inserted between a rotating shaft and a hub (such as a gear, pulley, flywheel, or pump impeller) to transmit rotational torque while preventing relative rotation between the two parts. Keyways are machined axial slots in both the shaft exterior and hub interior to accommodate the key body. Under load, transmitted torque induces a tangential driving force Ft at the shaft-hub interface. This force subjects the key to direct shear stress across its central horizontal plane (w × l) and bearing/crushing stress against the vertical sides of the keyways ((h/2) × l). Failure in shear results in total key shearing, while crushing failure leads to localized plastic deformation, keyway widening, backlash, and severe vibration.

working-principle.title: Working Principle
working-principle.prompt: Explain the mechanical force path and stress states in a shaft-hub-key connection during torque transmission.

mcq.question: For a standard square key where width b = h, what is the theoretical ratio of crushing stress to shear stress under pure torque transmission?
options: Crushing stress is equal to shear stress (sigma_c / tau = 1.0)
Crushing stress is twice the shear stress (sigma_c / tau = 2.0)
Crushing stress is half the shear stress (sigma_c / tau = 0.5)
Crushing stress is four times the shear stress (sigma_c / tau = 4.0)
mcq.answer: Crushing stress is twice the shear stress (sigma_c / tau = 2.0)

design-requirements.title: Design Requirements
given: Key Material: Plain Carbon Steel C45 (Syt = 360 MPa, Sut = 600 MPa)
Key Proportions (Square Key): Width b = 10 mm, Height h = 10 mm

engineering-assumptions.title: Engineering Assumptions
engineering-assumptions.prompt: Record key engineering assumptions for static key design under torque transmission.
questions: 1. State assumptions regarding uniform distribution of tangential force along the key length.
2. State assumptions regarding keyway fit, stress concentration at keyway ends, and key material isotropy.
3. State assumptions regarding allowable shear and crushing stress limits relative to yield strength.

key-design-calculation.title: Key Design Calculation
given: Power P = 22 kW, Speed N = 1440 rpm, Shaft Diameter d = 40 mm
Formula: Transmitted Torque T = (60 * 10^6 * P) / (2 * pi * N) N-mm
Formula: Tangential Force Ft = (2 * T) / d N
Formula: Minimum Length for Shear l_shear = (2 * T) / (d * b * tau_allow) mm
Formula: Minimum Length for Crushing l_crush = (4 * T) / (d * h * sigma_c_allow) mm
key-design-calculation.expectedProcess: Torque T = 145,887 N-mm. Tangential Force Ft = 7,294 N. Min required length for FOS=2.5 is l = 10.13 mm.

failure-analysis-safety.title: Failure Analysis & Safety Verification
given: Installed Key: Square Key b = 10 mm, h = 10 mm, Length l = 45 mm
Transmitted Torque T = 145,887 N-mm, Shaft Diameter d = 40 mm
Formula: Actual Shear Stress tau_act = (2 * T) / (d * b * l) MPa
Formula: Actual Crushing Stress sigma_c_act = (4 * T) / (d * h * l) MPa
Key Material C45: Syt = 360 MPa, Ssy = 0.5 * Syt = 180 MPa
Formula: Factor of Safety (FOS) = Ssy / tau_act or Syt / sigma_c_act
failure-analysis-safety.expectedProcess: Actual Shear Stress tau_act = 16.21 MPa. Actual Crushing Stress sigma_c_act = 32.42 MPa. FOS = 11.1 (or 4.44 relative to design allowable).

engineering-decision.title: Engineering Decision & Design Improvement
options: SAFE - Installed key (10 x 10 x 45 mm) provides adequate shear and crushing strength with high FOS
UNSAFE - Installed key will fail due to excessive shear or crushing stress under operating load
engineering-decision.prompt: Evaluate the safety of the installed key (10 x 10 x 45 mm) and provide your engineering decision with technical justification.

design-recommendation.title: Engineering Report & Reflection
design-recommendation.prompt: Synthesize your technical findings and answer the engineering reflection questions.
questions: 1. Summarize the key design verification (Torque T, Tangential Force Ft, Actual Stresses, and FOS).
2. Explain why a square key designed with b = h experiences equal factors of safety in shear and crushing when Ssy = 0.5 Syt.
3. Recommend keyway chamfering/fillet tolerances and material selection to mitigate fretting corrosion in industrial pump drives.
